statement: In bpp_offline_reorder_repack, a score_item that ranks items by size-descending but breaks near-ties using how tightly the residual capacity closes (favour sizes with small capacity-mod residues, i.e. items that can pair exactly to fill a bin) reduces bin count versus pure size-descending, with the largest effect on the size=50 and size=100 regimes where VBS relative gap is highest (2.30% / 2.20%).
rationale: Archive shows both frontier solvers are pure-priority reorder/repack variants with sub-millisecond runtimes (0.29-0.60 ms) and only 3/36 complementary wins, i.e. the search is dominated by a single ordering bias. Reordering priority is the only free lever in the allowed template, and the weakest regimes are the small/medium sizes where residue structure (mod capacity) most affects perfect packing opportunities.
